trip.title: Costa Rica, 5 nights · 1/6–1/11
trip.subtitle: Leave the Toronto snow behind and fly south into high summer on the Pacific. Two nights to the sound of the waves in Coco Bay: a boat out to snorkel, the sun going down into the bay, and on a new-moon night the whole sky of stars over the sand. Then around the lake to three nights at the foot of Arenal volcano, hot springs right outside the door. Float down a river past sloths dozing in the branches and crocodiles sunning on the banks, cross hanging bridges through the forest, ride out for a view of the volcano. After dark, walk into the rainforest with a flashlight and listen to it wake up. On the last full day, let a whole afternoon drift by in the warm river at Tabacón.
trip.notice: Nothing is booked yet. Flight and hotel prices were re-checked on Nov 15 for 1/6–1/11; for the rental car we only have the rules and daily insurance rates, so the car price is an estimate. USD converted at the Bank of Canada rate of 2026-11-13 (1 USD = 1.4257 CAD); Costa Rica's VAT is 13%. January is local school holidays, so beaches are still fairly busy around 1/6.
constraints: No surfing. Her Achilles is in late-stage rehab (already jogging and doing weight training), so regular tours are fine; just take a little care on rocky paths, getting on and off boats, and horseback riding
Driver is 23 at time of travel · Canadian G licence
Finish long and mountain drives in daylight (sunset ~17:30); at night only short drives of a few km in town

days.title: Wed · Nonstop to Liberia, sunset on the beach in Coco

schedule.title: Arrive at Pearson Terminal 3
schedule.text: Arrive 3 hours early for international flights. Partner: bring Chinese passport, US visa (confirm it's multiple-entry, M) and PR card.

schedule.title: Porter nonstop departs
schedule.text: About 5h 44m. Costa Rica is 1 hour behind Toronto.

schedule.title: Land in Liberia
schedule.text: Get the entry stamp (check it's in your passport), collect bags, then head to the Adobe shuttle stop.

schedule.title: Pick up the car
schedule.text: Bring your physical licence, passport, and a credit card in the driver's name (deposit ~USD1,000). Inspect the car and take photos; check by hand that the doors are locked, as rental car break-ins are common here.

schedule.title: Check in at Playas del Coco
schedule.text: About 30 min, arrive before dark.

schedule.title: Sunset on the beach
schedule.text: The beach in front of the hotel faces west, so the sun sets right over the water.

schedule.title: Seafood by the sea
schedule.text: Walk into Coco town (~15 min): Papagayo Seafood (often live music) or Mar Azul; take a taxi back if you don't feel like walking. If it's clear after dinner, stargaze for a bit on the beach in front of the hotel (no moon these nights); the proper stargazing night is tomorrow's new moon.

days.title: Thu · Drive to the catamaran snorkel trip, seafood in Coco and stargazing on the beach at night

schedule.title: Drive to the boardwalk
schedule.text: About 5 min; park on the street in town or in a paid lot. Leave nothing in the car, and pull the door handle to make sure it's locked.

schedule.title: Catamaran check-in
schedule.text: Marlin del Rey's 8:00 morning departure, about 4 hours: one snorkel stop, lunch, open bar. Strong Papagayo winds often pick up on dry-season afternoons, so the morning trip means calmer water. Boarding depends on the operator (sometimes you wade from the beach to a small shuttle boat), so ask before booking and get a hand from the crew if needed.

links.label: Marlin del Rey
Alternative: Tour Guanacaste morning catamaran · from USD79 · 8:00–12:00, leaves from Flamingo (about 1 hour drive from Coco)
Alternative: Blue Marlin private Papagayo catamaran · 8:00–12:00 · priced per boat (about USD400 for 5), pricey for two

schedule.title: Stroll around Coco
schedule.text: Lunch was on the boat; walk the boardwalk and grab some ice cream.

schedule.title: Back to the hotel to rest
schedule.text: 5 min drive back to the hotel: pool, nap.

schedule.title: Dinner: Coco town
schedule.text: Papagayo Seafood or Mar Azul; ~15 min walk or 5 min drive.

schedule.title: Stargazing on the beach (new moon)
schedule.text: 1/7 is exactly the new moon, so there's no moonlight all night; Guanacaste's dry season has lots of clear skies, and it's fully dark by 19:00. Right in front of the hotel is the darker north end of Coco beach: walk a little away from the streetlights and lie on a towel. Orion is high in the southeast, and the brightest star below it is Sirius; after 21:00, look low in the south for Canopus (the second-brightest star in the night sky, not visible from Toronto). Point Stellarium or SkyView on your phone at the sky to identify stars. Bring only your phone and a towel, no valuables, and don't wander far.

links.label: Moon phases (timeanddate)

days.title: Fri · Waterfall on the way, around Lake Arenal, hot springs in the afternoon, night walk in the evening

schedule.title: Check out and hit the road
schedule.text: Bring some cash (the waterfall is cash only).

schedule.title: Llanos de Cortés waterfall
schedule.text: About 30 concrete steps with a rope handrail; sandy at the bottom, rocky at the edge and in the water. You can take a dip; watch your step on the rocks so you don't roll an ankle.

schedule.title: Via Cañas and Tilarán to Lake Arenal
schedule.text: Lunch in Cañas or Tilarán. Between Cañas and Tilarán, don't follow the GPS left onto the dirt-road shortcut.

schedule.title: North shore of Lake Arenal
schedule.text: Drive the winding Route 142 and stop at roadside viewpoints for photos of the lake and volcano.

schedule.title: Check in at Termales del Arenal
schedule.text: All driving done in daylight. Once the room is ready, head straight for the hotel's hot-spring pools.

schedule.title: Soak in the hotel hot springs
schedule.text: Soak for a while; be ready to go by 17:00.

schedule.title: Drive to Bogarín
schedule.text: About 10 min, all in town, easy driving just after dark.

schedule.title: Bogarín night walk
schedule.text: A guide leads with a flashlight to find nocturnal frogs, snakes, scorpions and spiders, plus sleeping birds and sloths. The path is mostly flat; wear closed-toe shoes and bring a light jacket and bug spray. Start time per your booking.

links.label: Bogarín Trail
Alternative: Mistico night walk · USD54 + tax · starts 18:00, about 2.5 hours
Alternative: Ecocentro Danaus night walk · starts 17:30, about 2 hours, flat trail
Alternative: Fortuna Welcome night hike with wood-fired dinner · USD100 with transfers · leaves 16:30, about 4 hours

schedule.title: Dinner in town, drive back to the hotel
schedule.text: Snapper's House is right downtown; 5 min drive back to the hotel afterwards.

days.title: Sat · River float for sloths and crocodiles, hanging bridges in the afternoon

schedule.title: Early volcano viewing
schedule.text: The volcano is most likely to show itself 6–9 am, and you can see it from the hotel.

schedule.title: Peñas Blancas safari float
schedule.text: Hotel pickup; you sit in an inflatable raft steered by the guide, with little or no paddling (some operators ask for a few light strokes), for about 2 hours spotting sloths, monkeys, caimans and birds; back around 11:00. You get on and off at the riverbank, which may be muddy and rocky, so watch your step and wear non-slip, closed-toe water shoes.

links.label: Fortuna Welcome safari float · USD70 with transfers · leaves 7:30, about 4 hours
Alternative: Desafío safari float · USD72 + tax with transfers · starts 8:00, about 3 hours, some light paddling
Alternative: Two Weeks in Costa Rica safari float · USD69 + tax from January, with transfers · leaves 7:30, about 4.5 hours

schedule.title: Lunch in town
schedule.text: Ceviche at Cevichería D'Mora.

schedule.title: Mistico Hanging Bridges Park
schedule.text: About 25 min drive. 3.2 km loop with gentle slopes and steps; the hanging bridges sway; ~2 hours. Tag along behind a guided group and you'll often spot small creatures like eyelash vipers. Watch your footing on the slopes. Last entry 15:50.

links.label: Mistico official site
Alternative: Mistico guided natural history walk · USD44 + tax · about 2.5 hours, a guide spots wildlife for you
Alternative: Fortuna Welcome hanging bridges tour · USD70 with transfers and entry · leaves 14:00, about 4 hours
Alternative: Sky Adventures hanging bridges (El Castillo, about 40 minutes by car) · booking required

schedule.title: Back to the hotel for the hot springs
schedule.text: After the bridges, soak for a while before heading out to dinner.

schedule.title: Dinner in town
schedule.text: 5 min drive to town: Snapper's House (marlin ceviche, seafood soup) or Cevichería D'Mora; drive back to the hotel afterwards.

days.title: Sun · Morning horseback ride with volcano views, Tabacón from noon to early evening

schedule.title: Hotel pickup (horseback tour)
schedule.text: The volcano is most likely to be visible in the morning.

schedule.title: Horseback ride with Arenal Volcano views
schedule.text: About 2.5 hours of riding through forest and pasture to a volcano viewpoint and Los Lirios lake; the guide gives a lesson first. Note: keeping heels down in the stirrups and pushing off one foot to mount and dismount put some strain on the Achilles; if it feels tight, keep the horse at a walk.

links.label: Fortuna Welcome horseback tour
Alternative: Mistico Paco’s Horses ride · USD58 + tax · starts 8:15, about 2.5 hours, crosses a river on horseback
Alternative: Don Tobias ride to a volcano lookout · starts 8:30, about 3 hours, transfers included, ask for the price

schedule.title: Back to the hotel to change
Tabacón hot river + lunch
schedule.text: About 10 min drive. Hot rivers, waterfalls and gardens at the foot of the volcano; the day pass includes lunch. The natural pools in the river have rocky bottoms; the flat-bottomed built pools are steadier. Still lovely in the rain. Leave at 17:00 and get back to the hotel before dark.

schedule.title: Dinner at the hotel
schedule.text: Eat at the hotel, or drive 5 min into town.

days.title: Mon · Drive back to Liberia, nonstop flight home

schedule.title: One last look at the volcano, breakfast
Head to the airport
schedule.text: Along the lake via Tilarán and Cañas, about 3 hours on the road; allow time to fill up (the car must be returned full) and arrive by 12:00.

schedule.title: Return the car, shuttle to the airport
schedule.text: The departure tax is usually included in the airfare.

schedule.title: Porter nonstop back to Toronto
schedule.text: Arrive 20:58. Partner shows PR card when entering Canada.

coverage.note: About 530 steps down, and the climb back up is harder; not great value just for a look at the falls.

coverage.item: Arenal 1968 lava trails / national park trails
coverage.note: These are hiking trails; enjoying volcano views from the lake and the hotel instead.

coverage.item: Rincón de la Vieja mud bath and hot springs
coverage.note: About 1 hour from Hermosa; Guachipelín hot springs + volcanic mud USD45. For an extra soak, fit it into the afternoon of 1/7. The mud bath area is reached on a stretch of dirt path, so ask about conditions before going.

coverage.item: Palo Verde boat tour for crocodiles
coverage.note: Overlaps with the Peñas Blancas float; private tour USD178 + tax, fairly pricey.
Day passes are paused for the Christmas season until 1/5 and available from 1/6; the hotel's own hot springs plus optional Tabacón are plenty.
No surfing; Tamarindo is 1.5 hours from the airport and mostly about surfing and nightlife.
Same route; flights with carry-on cost about CA$670 more, but hotels like Villa del Sueño have availability.
Termales del Arenal has its own hot-spring pools and is right next door to Ecotermales; for a change of scene, go during the day (10:00–16:00 session).
The night walk shows you more animals; the morning of 1/10 is now horseback riding.

coverage.item: Other spots from the RedNote posts
coverage.note: Poás Volcano, La Paz Waterfall Gardens and the Starbucks coffee farm are near San José, 2–3 hours from La Fortuna; Maquique canyoning and the Finca Modelo tree climb aren't suitable for Achilles rehab; Monteverde is too far to fit into five nights.

Late-stage rehab, already jogging and weight training: all the regular tours are included; rocky paths, boarding boats and horseback riding are flagged with 'take care' in the itinerary. La Fortuna Waterfall (~530 steps, mixed reviews in the posts) is not scheduled.
The long legs (airport to Coco, Coco to the volcano, volcano back to the airport) are all in daylight; at night only 3–10 min drives in town (Coco, La Fortuna).

rental.title: Car rental: pick up 1/6 16:15 – return 1/11 12:00 (5 days)
rental.summary: There's no convenient public transit between the two regions, so we drive all five days. Recommended: Adobe, minimum age 23 with no young-driver fee; pick-up and return are at the office outside the airport, with a free shuttle.

notes: Mandatory third-party liability (TPL/SLI) can't be waived, and most low prices on third-party sites exclude it; go by the rental office's quote.
Other companies: Vamos also has no young-driver fee; Europcar charges USD6/day; Alamo, Enterprise and National charge drivers aged 21–24 but don't publish the amount.

events.title: Papagayo winds
events.description: From December to April, strong winds often blow across the Gulf of Papagayo, usually lasting a few days and stronger in the afternoon.
events.conflict: Take the morning catamaran; if it's cancelled for wind, switch to the Rincón de la Vieja mud bath and hot springs (day trip, ~1 hour drive).

events.title: 1/7 New moon · stargazing
events.description: Almost no moonlight on the nights of 1/6–1/10. Guanacaste's dry season has lots of clear skies: on 1/7, stargaze from the north end of the beach in front of the Coco hotel; look up during the 1/8 night walk too; on other nights, stargaze from the hotel hot springs, though Arenal is often cloudy, so it's down to luck.
events.conflict: No driving: walk to the beach in front of the hotel; bring only your phone and a towel.

events.title: Santa Cruz / Palmares festivals
events.description: The Santa Cruz traditional festival is usually 1/14–1/18, and the Palmares festival runs mid-to-late January; both are after this trip.

items.title: Confirm your Canadian passport is valid for the whole trip
items.note: Canadian citizens are visa-free for up to 180 days; make sure you get an entry stamp in your passport. Bring your return itinerary.

items.title: Confirm visa-free entry: US visa is multiple-entry, or bring Canadian PR card
items.note: Chinese passports are in Group 3 (visa required), but holders of a valid US multiple-entry visa or Canadian permanent residency are exempt (new rule from 2025-11: at least 1 day of validity left on entry, and the stay can't go beyond that validity). The official site couldn't be fetched automatically, so check the immigration page in a browser before departure or ask the airline.

cash.summary: Hotels, tours, gas stations and most restaurants take cards (Visa/Mastercard). Cash is only needed for the items below: US dollars mainly for tips and emergencies, colones for small places that only take local currency. Most of it is already counted in the food and tickets budgets; tips of about US$45 come out of the buffer.

currencies.label: US dollars
currencies.how: Exchange CAD at a Canadian bank or currency exchange before leaving. Get small, crisp, undamaged bills (damaged US bills are often refused locally): $1×10, $5×6, $10×3, $20×4.

currencies.label: Costa Rican colones
currencies.how: Don't exchange in Canada. After landing, withdraw about ₡30,000 from a bank ATM (BCR, BN, BAC) in the Liberia Airport arrivals hall or in Coco or La Fortuna; some ATMs don't work from 11 pm to 5 am.

items.label: Llanos de Cortés waterfall entry
items.note: ₡4,000/person, cash only (1/8)

items.label: Parking attendants (cuidacarros)
items.note: Informal attendants watch cars at beaches and on town streets, ₡500–1,000 each time

items.label: Sodas, fruit stands, ice cream
items.note: Small shops may not take cards; already in the food budget

items.label: Evening taxi in Coco (optional)
items.note: Taxi from town back to Villa Del Sol if you don't feel like walking, about ₡2,000 per ride

items.label: Tips for guides and crew
items.note: About US$10 each for the catamaran, float and sloth guides; a few dollars for shuttle drivers

items.label: Housekeeping tips
items.note: About US$2/night × 5 nights; restaurant bills already include a 10% service charge, so no extra tip needed

items.label: Emergency cash
items.note: For when cards or ATMs don't work; bring it home if unused

tips: Exchange rate about ₡450 = US$1 (Nov 2026); US$1 is about 1.4257 CAD (Bank of Canada, 11/13).
US dollars are accepted everywhere, but change often comes back in colones at a poor rate; paying in colones at small places is better value.
When the card machine asks whether to pay in CAD or colones, choose colones (local currency); don't let the merchant convert it to CAD.
Use a credit card with no foreign transaction fee; ATM withdrawals charge a fee, so take out enough at once rather than several times.
